reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it actively promotes paid BitClub mining and investment packages by presenting recurring, passive and potentially very large earnings as membership benefits. The presenters urge viewers to purchase packages, recruit friends and join a network, including claims of daily payments, passive income and a possible large payday from CoinPay. The webinar is therefore a solicitation for participation in an earnings scheme, not merely a neutral explanation of Bitcoin mining.

citations.quote: You are paid today. You can do your withdrawal today.
you can purchase all your money but only part
one player will enter the freehand in the left foot and the other in the right leg
You will be able to access the business academy in a closed system, after your payment is made
for more than two years and two months in this project I received passive income

opening.argument: Judge, the financial discussion includes uncertainty that matters. The speaker says Bitcoin will not rise forever and compares it to a stock or commodity. He also acknowledges that the Zcash results disappointed them and that mining blocks can arrive unevenly. Those are material risks to someone evaluating mining income, not a claim that every participant's return is fixed or guaranteed. The daily-payment statement should be weighed alongside these admissions rather than read as a promise that mining economics cannot change.

citations.quote: I don't think it will always grow upward. I can even say that I know that it will not grow up forever. It's the same as any other stock or commodity
That has not gone even as close to as well as we thought it was going to go We're actually really disappointed in the results from that
on the days we had hours when we couldn't lock the block at all and then we locked 2 blocks in a row

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited withdrawal line describes what a member can do today; it does not specify a future rate or guarantee. The passive-income line reports one person's past experience, while the paid-access line concerns an academy. Even the cited package wording does not, by itself, establish that the payment purchases a guaranteed mining return. The opening omits the speaker's explicit acknowledgment that Bitcoin will not keep rising.

citations.quote: You are paid today. You can do your withdrawal today.
I can even say that I know that it will not grow up forever.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Acknowledging price swings does not undo the solicitation. The presentation connects purchasable packages to profit and invites viewers to start the business, while a presenter offers his passive income as an example. No fixed rate is needed for the paid mining-income pitch to be the central concern.

citations.quote: These all tickets costs between $500 and $2000 and all that makes this package also profitable
for more than two years and two months in this project I received passive income.
now we hit the button Start business click this button

opening.argument: Judge, much of this webinar functions as a live explanation of mining and the business's operations. Questions address whether mining will end, where equipment is located, and whether the company is audited. The speaker also walks through block rewards, fees, electricity and maintenance when explaining profitability. That question-and-answer setting gives the earnings discussion an operational context: viewers are hearing how the speakers calculate and assess mining, not just an isolated invitation to pay.

citations.quote: The question 1 was, will Bitcoin mining ever finish Bitcoin and what will happen then.
Second, where are the facilities with the equipment, mining equipment... Third, do you have audit of the company...
In each block is about 12 & a half new bitcoins plus its fees
our electricity and maintenance is $400,000 per month

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution selects payment, packages and recruitment from a longer discussion that also takes questions about mining and auditing. A paid academy can be training, and the quoted account of passive income is personal experience; neither quote alone proves that the explanations are a pretext. The block-reward and expense calculation gives viewers something concrete to examine rather than merely asking them to trust a payout claim.

citations.quote: Third, do you have audit of the company...
In each block is about 12 & a half new bitcoins plus its fees
our electricity and maintenance is $400,000 per month

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The questions and calculations do not make this a neutral lesson. The same presentation turns mining figures into a profit claim, presents paid packages as profitable, and closes with an instruction to start the business. Operational detail can support a sales pitch; it does not erase one.

citations.quote: So that's a profit of $2.5 million That's income, monthly income, that's $2.5 million
These all tickets costs between $500 and $2000 and all that makes this package also profitable
now we hit the button Start business click this button

opening.argument: Judge, the offer can be read as a membership business selling access and equipment-related packages. The speaker describes buying hardware, adding mining equipment, and giving members ClubCoin and CoinPay shares. The record does not show the actual purchase terms or a schedule promising each buyer a specified return. Nor does the quoted binary-plan passage establish that either named recruit paid or that the speaker received a commission from them. Price, member benefits and a referral structure warrant scrutiny, but they do not by themselves establish what any purchaser was contractually promised.

citations.quote: you can directly buy the hardware that will help you increase your profit.
We keep expanding the mining operation to make it bigger and bigger and bigger
We give out free ClubCoin and offer free CoinPay shares.
Binar is made in a way that you will have enough of 2 players for a complete bonus

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's excerpts establish promotion, not the precise terms of a deceptive transaction. The cited passive-income statement is a speaker's own history; the academy quote identifies paid training; and the binary passage is difficult to interpret without the surrounding plan. The presentation also describes hardware and added equipment, so the package references need not mean payment for a promised return alone.

citations.quote: you can directly buy the hardware that will help you increase your profit.
I mean how we mine more and more equipment and add more things like free ClubCoin, free shares in CoinPay.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a contract or completed transaction does not change what is being promoted. Viewers are offered priced packages described as profitable, told about daily payments and passive income, and shown a bonus structure tied to bringing in people. Hardware and member perks are presented within that paid earnings opportunity, not separately from it.
